overall_assessment: All 28 packet courses were reviewed, including all 20 suspects and eight random controls; no personal-data leak was confirmed in the displayed material, and coordinator names are correctly removed in both suspects and controls. Most flags are false alarms: name_like hits are course/programme titles or technical terms, high removed shares reflect legitimate administrative-year removal from very short records, and the admin_date flags identify government-document dates that must stay; the two phone-flagged plans have truncated reference lists and show no identifiable contact number in their displayed text. One artifact flag exposes genuine reference-URL damage from removing a publication date; semicolon-related removed spans otherwise preserve the words, and the control containing cohort years uses them to identify the students to whom assessment instructions apply.

findings.description: The date 01.12.2016 is removed from the filename of the Riksarkivet Noark 5 standard cited in the syllabus. This is a document/publication date in a literature reference, not administrative dating of the course; deleting it leaves empty parentheses inside the URL and changes the reference link. This explains the artifact flag and is the only confirmed content damage in the packet.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: R/anonymize.R: the generic dd.mm.yyyy removal in .anon_generic() can match a date inside a parenthesized URL filename because its preceding-character guard excludes digits, dots and slashes but not an opening parenthesis. The government-document guard only examines the preceding 80 characters, and the reference title is much farther away in this long URL.
findings.suggested_fix: Protect complete URL tokens from generic date removal, or exclude matches whose positions fall inside URL spans, while retaining removal of administrative dates outside links. Add a regression case for the exact Noark filename containing (01.12.2016).pdf and require the complete URL to remain unchanged.
